OpenGWASDB ukb-b Dense Store — Performance & Validation

Genome-wide · 2,514 UK Biobank analyses · observed-only and reference-completed

Published

August 23, 2026

ImportantMeasured at format_version 0.1, not re-run for the z or eaf encodings

Every figure below was measured against stores whose z plane is float16 and which carry no eaf at all. Two changes have landed since, both of which move stored size and add a decode step to every read: issue #114 (ADR 0037 §1) made z int16 fixed point with an exact overflow table, and issue #116 (ADR 0037 §2, §4) made eaf a per-variant baseline plus an int8 logit residual and moved format_version to 2.0. The sizes and timings here describe neither. They are re-measured against rebuilt stores in #117, before the version that ships the encodings is cut (CONTRIBUTING.md, “Benchmarks are measurements, not prose”).

Overview

Two Dense stores over the 2,514 genome-wide UK Biobank GWAS in the OpenGWAS ukb-b batch:

  • an Observed-Only store built from the source GWAS-VCFs with inline hg19→hg38 liftover;
  • a Reference-Completed store whose variant axis is the observed source variants plus EUR LD-panel variants.

This report benchmarks query latency across all access patterns, storage and build cost versus the raw VCFs, and an MR IVW analysis as an end-to-end scientific validation.

Property Observed-Only Reference-Completed
Analyses (GWAS) 2,514 2,514
Variants (hg38) 9,847,701 11,192,757
Additional panel variants — 1,345,056
Associations (dense cells) 24.8 billion 28.1 billion
Reference assembly GRCh38 GRCh38

Storage vs. raw VCF

Form Files Size
Raw source VCFs (.vcf.gz) 2,514 files 425.4 GB
OpenGWASDB Dense Observed-Only single store 58.0 GB
OpenGWASDB Dense Reference-Completed single store 75.2 GB

7.3× smaller than the source VCFs (58.0 GB vs 425 GB) — one queryable store replacing 2,514 files. The store keeps float16 z + se, a tabix variant axis, an mmap’d ALID index, and a top-hit index.

The reference-completed store is 17.2 GB larger than observed-only after adding 1,345,056 panel variants, imputed flags, and completion metadata.

Query performance

Median of repeated calls after one warm-up, on the full genome-wide stores.

Pattern Observed median Completed median Completed / observed Result cells What it reads
bulk 29.65 s 35.57 s 1.20× 8,419,893 → 10,003,315 One analysis, all variants (analysis)
phewas 5.3 ms 9.7 ms 1.84× 1,344 → 2,514 One variant × all 2,514 analyses (phewas)
regional 620.7 ms 948.3 ms 1.53× 5,231,847 → 9,669,654 All associations in a 1 Mb window (range_phewas)
tophits 1.2 ms 1.8 ms 1.52× 7,390 → 8,580 Significant hits for ukb-b-10912 (addressed index slice, p<5e-8)
random_lookup 814.7 ms 679.2 ms 0.83× 566 → 909 100 variants × 10 analyses (lookup)

phewas and the analysis-addressed top_hits call are low-millisecond point queries. bulk and regional scale with the number of cells returned. Top-hit tiers are packed by analysis index and canonical genomic position, with an offset table mapping each analysis directly to one contiguous slice. The reference-completed index stores the imputed flag alongside z/se, avoiding random reads into data.zarr/imputed.

random_lookup across request sizes

The table above reports one fixed random_lookup shape (100 variants × 10 analyses). The table below re-measures lookup on the observed-only store across four request shapes, with no competing background job on the host, to separate the row-axis cost (scattered variants, each its own row-chunk) from the column-axis cost (requested analyses).

Variants Analyses Cells requested Median p95 Result cells
1 1 1 2.3 ms 3.5 ms 1
100 10 1,000 777.9 ms 945.5 ms 553
10 100 1,000 100.0 ms 103.7 ms 499
100 500 50,000 898.0 ms 929.3 ms 29,153

7 repetitions per shape after one warm-up, store: /data/opengwasdb/wip/ukb-b.opengwasdb.

Latency tracks the number of scattered row-chunks touched, not the number of requested cells: 100 variants × 10 analyses (777.9 ms) and 100 variants × 500 analyses (898.0 ms) cost almost the same despite a 50× difference in requested cells, because both scatter 100 variants across 100 separate row-chunks. 10 variants × 100 analyses (100.1 ms) is far cheaper with the same 1,000 requested cells, because it only touches 10 row-chunks. The single-cell lookup (2.3 ms) is close to the store’s point-query floor. This is the read pattern issue opengwasdb#52 targets: lookup currently reads full analysis-width column-chunks per selected row rather than only the column-chunks intersecting the requested analyses.

Analysis-major top-hit experiment

The previous implementation materialised the complete 5.5–6.4 million-entry tier and filtered it in Python. The experiment below holds the analysis, threshold, result ordering, and result count constant while varying only the one-dimensional Zarr chunk length. Each figure is based on 10 timed warm-cache repetitions after a warm-up. “First read” is reported separately as the first call after reopening the store; it is not claimed to be a controlled cold-cache measurement.

Observed-Only

Chunk First read Selected median Selected p95 Global median Index size Repack
1,024 2.7 ms 2.1 ms 2.2 ms 1.18 s 730.6 MB 70.8 s
4,096 2.1 ms 1.4 ms 1.4 ms 628.4 ms 700.5 MB 34.3 s
16,384 1.6 ms 1.2 ms 1.2 ms 488.1 ms 692.7 MB 16.0 s

Reference-Completed

Chunk First read Selected median Selected p95 Global median Index size Repack
1,024 3.3 ms 2.8 ms 3.0 ms 1.62 s 851.6 MB 91.6 s
4,096 2.3 ms 1.7 ms 1.7 ms 820.3 ms 814.0 MB 43.8 s
16,384 2.5 ms 1.8 ms 1.8 ms 608.9 ms 803.1 MB 19.5 s

The selected 16,384-entry chunk keeps the completed selected-analysis read within 10% of its absolute fastest trial while materially improving global-read latency; it is also the fastest configuration for the observed store. Observed latency fell from 304.4 ms to 1.17 ms (261×), and completed latency from 397.9 ms to 1.77 ms (225×). Both comfortably meet the under-10-ms target, and every measured selected result exactly matched its corresponding global subset. The indexes grew to 692.7 MB and 803.1 MB respectively; this experiment deliberately prioritised latency over space.

MR validation: imputed high cholesterol → heart attack

An end-to-end inverse-variance weighted (IVW) Mendelian randomization run straight off the store, as a scientific smoke test. For the reference-completed store this deliberately uses only imputed instruments: the exposure top-hit association must be imputed, and the exposure/outcome lookup used in the scatter plot is also restricted to instruments where both cells are imputed.

  • Exposure (ukb-b-10912): Non-cancer illness code, self-reported: high cholesterol
  • Outcome (ukb-b-11590): Vascular/heart problems diagnosed by doctor: Heart attack
  • Observed-only reference: genome-wide significant (p<5e-8) exposure variants, distance-pruned at 1000 kb → 66 instruments from 7,390 raw hits.
  • Reference-completed sanity check: imputed-only genome-wide significant exposure variants, distance-pruned at 1000 kb → 49 instruments from 1,190 imputed raw hits (8,580 total exposure hits before filtering).

Effects are already on the same allele (the store orients every analysis to the canonical ALID), so no harmonisation step is needed. Both traits are binary, so effects are log odds ratios.

Quantity Observed-Only Completed: imputed-only
IVW estimate (log OR / log-OR exposure) 0.115 0.110
Standard error 0.005 0.006
Z 21.37 18.43
P-value 2.59e-101 8.11e-76

The imputed-only estimate is positive — genetically higher cholesterol liability is associated with higher heart-attack risk, the expected direction for this positive-control sanity check.

Regional imputation sanity check

The 1 Mb regional check is centred on the strongest imputed high-cholesterol top hit in the completed store. The plot shows all high-cholesterol associations returned for that window, with imputed associations highlighted.

  • Analysis: ukb-b-10912 (Non-cancer illness code, self-reported: high cholesterol)
  • Region: chr19:44,409,976-45,409,976 centred on 19:44909976:G:T (z=28.53)
  • Associations plotted: 4,017 total; 3,302 observed and 715 imputed.

  • Data: opengwasdb_ukbb_dense_benchmark.json and opengwasdb_ukbb_dense_completed_benchmark.json (from benchmarks/benchmark_ukbb_dense.py)
  • Store: /local-scratch/data/opengwas/opengwasdb/ukb-b.opengwasdb (9,847,701 × 2,514)
  • Completed store: /local-scratch/data/opengwas/opengwasdb/ukb-b-c128-completed.opengwasdb (11,192,757 × 2,514)
  • MR is a demonstration/validation of the query layer, not a definitive epidemiological estimate (self-reported binary exposure, distance-based pruning in place of LD clumping).
